//: Lighthouse CI config. Runs against the built static output so dev-server SSR quirks never affect scores. The url list is EXPLICIT on purpose: with staticDistDir alone, lhci auto-discovers pages but caps at maxAutodiscoverUrls (default 5), so it was testing a near-random 5 of 22 pages, including the /404 page and the Google Search Console verification stub (googlebc11aa9bca0fae39.html), which dragged the accessibility gate below 100. Listing the urls disables auto-discovery (lhci still serves staticDistDir and swaps in its own port), so the run covers every distinct template and skips the non-page stub. One case study stands in for all ten since they share a layout; /coming-soon is its own standalone template. Accessibility is a hard gate (the site holds 100 and that bar must not regress), as are LCP under 4.5s and CLS under 0.1 (family standard, 2026-09-06); performance / best-practices / SEO scores and total byte weight are warnings so normal CI variance doesn't block a PR while still surfacing drops. Run locally with: npm run build && npx lhci autorun (see CLAUDE.md Gotcha 9: it does not complete on Nathan's Windows machine, trust the CI run)

assert.//: numberOfRuns is 3 and assertions use the MEDIAN, not a single sample. With one run, largest-contentful-paint as a hard error measures the CI runner as much as the site: on 2026-09-06 the identical commit passed on staging and failed on main at 6779ms against a 4500 budget, on a commit that only touched a workflow file. A gate that cries wolf gets ignored, and an ignored gate is worse than none. Three runs cost roughly 3x the job time, which is the price of the timing assertions being trustworthy.
